text:
Alex: thinking out loud 1 — add a tiny "hotspot shepherd" optimization to reduce rehydrate thrash for a handful of ultra-hot prefixes
Maria: what's the shepherd invariant?
Alex: its a cooperative token (no heavy fencing). encodes level, epoch, last-write-hash. readers can short-circuit to local cache when epoch matches
Sam: sounds like soft-pin ++. how do we avoid violating read-after-write ordering?
Kevin: big worry is demote+write races and tombstone staleness. cooperative token can't be the sole source of truth
Alex: agreed. design: shepherd = optimization only. canonical correctness still uses leases + tombstone propagation. shepherd accelerates reads but writers bump epoch in coord layer and emit invalidate hooks
Sam: sketch of behavior: readers check epoch; if equal, serve. if mismatch, fetch from canonical path and refresh token. writers bump epoch and update last-write-hash; if hash mismatch then emit synchronous invalidate for affected slices
Alex: config I experimented with:
```
hotspot_shepherd:
  ttl_ms: 2500
  refresh_backoff_ms: 200
  levels:
    - name: warm
      grace_ms: 500
    - name: hot
      grace_ms: 2000
    - name: blazing
      grace_ms: 8000
```
Maria: fallback if holder node crashes? other nodes must not serve stale data that would break ordering
Kevin: fallback: on node loss, tokens expire fast and reads fall back to leases. Also require writers to perform epoch bump in coord so mismatch is immediately visible to new readers
Sam: eviction interaction: when token exists eviction should prefer non-shepherd slabs. but must be bounded
Alex: propose eviction_credit per token. each shepherd consumes credits; scheduler honors budgets so hotkeys don't starve others
Maria: tie credits to tenant SLA maybe. also add telemetry: token_hit_rate, invalidation_rate, stale_sample_count, evict_churn_per_key
Kevin: testing: 1) unit tests for epoch bump + read-after-write; 2) multi-node chaos (node crash during spike); 3) canary on low-traffic shard with strict gating
Sam: canary gate idea: 0.5% traffic, abort if >1% stale reads in 1s window or >5 errors or sustained p95 latency increase
ops-bot: canary scheduled cluster=canary-3 window=2h start=2026-04-02T03:00Z
Maria: runtime enable for Dedicated/Private: config toggle + console gate + SDK kill-switch so ops can flip remotely
Alex: I'll draft RFC with state machine: allocate -> refresh -> epoch-mismatch -> invalidate -> expire. will include reference impl in prefix layer
Kevin: include explicit invariants: "read reflects write within tombstone visibility bound" and "no silent demote violating ordering". enumerate failure modes and mitigating actions
Sam: I'll own chaos tests and canary harness
Maria: doc checklist: migration steps from soft-pin, dashboards, rollback playbook, KB for SRE on token metrics interpretation
Alex: thanks all. will post RFC link. cc @Sam @Kevin @Maria :thumbsup:
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sam: happy to help
Kevin: will sketch invariants tomorrow
